message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles using a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Go to [airnow.gov](https://www.airnow.gov/), enter “Los Angeles, CA” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and health advisories. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit [aqicn.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/). | Live AQI, trend graph, and forecast for the next 24 h. |
| **Local news or weather apps** | Many local stations (e.g., KABC, KNBC) display AQI on their weather pages. | Quick visual indicator (green, yellow, orange, red, etc.). |

**Typical LA air‑quality pattern**  
- **Spring & early summer**: Ozone levels often rise due to sunlight and traffic, especially on hot, dry days.  
- **Fall & winter**: Particulate matter (PM₂.₅) can spike from wild‑fire smoke or heating emissions.  
- **Weekends**: Traffic‑related pollutants may dip slightly, but overall trends depend on weather.

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI at least a few hours before you head out. If the AQI is above 100 (moderate or higher), consider wearing a mask or limiting strenuous exercise. For the most accurate, up‑to‑date numbers, use one of the links above.
